title: Uthai Thani 3-Day Itinerary — Riverside Town + Ban Rai Nature | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Uthai Thani itinerary covering the Sakae Krang riverside town, Trok Rong Ya, Khao Sakae Krang, Wat Tha Sung, then nature day in Ban Rai–Lan Sak: Hub Pa Tat, Wat Tham Khao Wong. With opening hours, distances, and real eats.
keywords: Uthai Thani 3 day itinerary, Uthai Thani trip plan, Hub Pa Tat, Ban Rai Uthai Thani, Wat Tham Khao Wong, Khao Sakae Krang, Wat Tha Sung
h1:
Uthai Thani in 3 Days, 2 Nights
Riverside Town + Ban Rai Nature & Hub Pa Tat
intro: Three days is just about right to see both sides of Uthai Thani. The town side is the Sakae Krang River, floating houses, a morning market that wakes before sunrise, the old Trok Rong Ya lane, and a temple on a hilltop. The other side is Ban Rai–Lan Sak, all limestone mountains, the Hub Pa Tat valley where you walk through a cave tunnel into a prehistoric forest, and Wat Tham Khao Wong, a teakwood temple tucked in a mountain valley. This plan keeps you in town for both nights and uses the middle day to drive out for nature without packing up. The timing is built around the real opening and closing hours of each spot.
chips: ⛩️ Wat Tha Sung, Wat Tham Khao Wong

blocks.html: Uthai Thani sits about 220 km from Bangkok, roughly a 3-hour drive up the Asia Highway (Route 32). The one thing to grasp before you plan is that the province's top sights are in different zones. The riverside town on the Sakae Krang and Wat Tha Sung are close together, short walks and short drives. But Hub Pa Tat is in Lan Sak district (about 28 km from town) and Wat Tham Khao Wong is in Ban Rai district (about 60 km from town). Three days and two nights works out nicely, because it leaves the middle day free to drive the nature route at a full, unhurried pace.

items: Day 1 — Riverside town Arrive around midday, walk Trok Rong Ya, eat giant gourami by the river, head up Khao Sakae Krang in the afternoon to pay respects at Wat Sangkat Rattana Khiri and wait for sunset, then stroll the riverside in the evening

Day 2 — Ban Rai–Lan Sak nature run Up early and out of town, walk through the cave at Hub Pa Tat to see the prehistoric forest, then on to Wat Tham Khao Wong with its teakwood hall in a mountain valley, back into town by evening

Day 3 — Morning market + Wat Tha Sung Up before dawn for the riverside morning market, eat rice congee and pa thong ko, head to Wat Tha Sung later to see the Glass Temple and the Golden Palace, then eat giant gourami at lunch before heading home
Where to stay Stay both nights in town by the Sakae Krang River. You can walk to the morning market and Trok Rong Ya, and you never have to move your bags even though the middle day takes you far out

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old town, Khao Sakae Krang, riverside sunset

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Trok Rong Ya · Khao Sakae Krang · riverside

items.activity: Arrive in Uthai Thani, check in to a Sakae Krang riverside stay
items.note: Leave Bangkok around 8am with a rest stop and you'll arrive right about midday. Drop your bags before heading out on foot.

items.activity: Riverside lunch — try the giant gourami Uthai Thani is known for
items.note: The giant gourami is raised in net pens on the Sakae Krang. The flesh is firm and not fishy, good fried, steamed, or blanched with a dipping sauce.

items.activity: Stroll Trok Rong Ya, the old Chinese quarter in the town center
items.note: A lane of old wooden houses with a few cafes, sweet shops, and scattered street art. It's quiet by day, easy walking and photos.

items.activity: Coffee break at a town cafe to dodge the afternoon heat
items.note: There are several small cafes around town, both along Trok Rong Ya and by the river. Pick one with a river view if you can.

items.activity: Drive up Khao Sakae Krang to Wat Sangkat Rattana Khiri
items.note: You can drive all the way to the top, or climb the 449-step naga staircase if you want the workout. Up top there are bells to ring and a replica Buddha footprint to pay respects to.

items.activity: Wait for sunset on the summit, 360-degree town view
items.note: From here you can see Uthai Thani town, the Sakae Krang River, and the rice fields all around. The color shift as the sky changes is the day's highlight.

items.activity: Head back down into town for dinner along the Sakae Krang
items.note: Several riverside spots stay open into the evening. With a cool breeze, it's an easy way to close out the first day.

blocks.title: A timing tip
blocks.html: Wat Sangkat Rattana Khiri on Khao Sakae Krang is the best sunset spot in town. Check that day's sunset time and head up about 45 minutes early, so you can both pay respects and claim your photo angle before the crowd arrives.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Ban Rai–Lan Sak nature run, Hub Pa Tat, Wat Tham Khao Wong

blocks.html: Today is the highlight of the three-day trip. You head west out of town into the mountain zone. The route from town to Hub Pa Tat runs along Route 333 then 3438, through Nong Chang to Lan Sak, about 28 km. Wat Tham Khao Wong is in Ban Rai district, a bit further out. Leaving early is the way to do both at a relaxed pace and catch cooler air for the forest walk.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Hub Pa Tat · Wat Tham Khao Wong · back to town by evening

items.activity: Quick breakfast in town, then set off for Lan Sak
items.note: Fill up the tank before you go, since gas stations are spread out in the Ban Rai–Lan Sak zone. Bring drinking water in the car too.

items.activity: Arrive at Hub Pa Tat in Lan Sak, walk through the cave into the prehistoric forest
items.note: Open 08:00–16:30. Entry for Thai adults 20 THB, children 10 THB. You walk through a short limestone cave tunnel and come out into a valley where light filters down, with fan palms growing thick like you've slipped into another era.

items.activity: Walk the valley trail, photograph the light coming through the cave opening
items.note: The paved path is easy walking, a loop of about 700 meters. Wear comfortable shoes. Mid-morning is when the light pours into the valley best.

items.activity: Leave Hub Pa Tat, drive on toward Ban Rai district
items.note: The drive runs past field and mountain views. You can stop for lunch at a local spot in Ban Rai town.

items.activity: Lunch in Ban Rai town
items.note: Ban Rai has local food and made-to-order shops to choose from. Refuel before heading up to the hillside temple.

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Tham Khao Wong, see the four-story teakwood hall in the valley
items.note: Open Mon–Fri 07:00–17:00, Sat–Sun 07:00–18:00. The Thai-style pavilion is built entirely from teak and makha wood, set against the limestone mountains. It's a calm, photogenic temple.

items.activity: Walk up to the cave above to pay respects to the Buddha image (about 400 meters)
items.note: The path up to the cave is a staircase, not a long climb. The cave is cool and pleasant. Dress modestly and remove your shoes where indicated.

items.activity: Leave the temple, drive back to Uthai Thani town
items.note: The return is about 60 km and takes around an hour and a half. Leaving before the light fades makes the drive easier.

items.activity: Back in town, relax, dinner along the Sakae Krang
items.note: It's been a lot of walking today, so keep dinner light by the river and save your energy for the early market tomorrow.

blocks.title: What to know before the nature day
blocks.html: Hub Pa Tat and Wat Tham Khao Wong are in different districts, both far from town. You'll need your own car or a rental today. Wear comfortable sneakers, bring drinking water, and note that if it rains the path through the Hub Pa Tat cave can get slippery. Check the weather before you go. In the rainy season the valley is lush and green but the footing is extra slick.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Riverside morning market + Wat Tha Sung before heading home

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Morning market · Wat Tha Sung · giant gourami to close

items.activity: Up before dawn for the morning market along the Sakae Krang
items.note: The market gets going from around 3am and winds down by 9am. Fresh produce, local fish, home-style dishes, old-fashioned sweets. Come early for the real feel of the town.

items.activity: Breakfast in the market — rice congee, pa thong ko, old-style coffee
items.note: Graze as you go, and try the Vietnamese kuai chap that pairs so well with Uthai Thani if you find a shop open.

items.activity: Back to the stay, pack up, check out
items.note: Once the market winds down the town quiets, which is a good window to head out to Wat Tha Sung before the sun gets harsh.

items.activity: Drive to Wat Tha Sung (Wat Chantharam), about 12 km from town
items.note: Take Route 3265, following signs toward Manorom district. Signs are posted the whole way. The temple opens 08:00–16:00.

items.activity: See the Glass Temple (the 100-meter hall), morning session 09:00–11:30
items.note: The interior is decorated with mirrored glass throughout until it shimmers, and holds the preserved body of Luang Por Ruesi Ling Dam. This room opens in sessions, so come in the morning to fit the timing.

items.activity: Walk through the Golden Palace and other temple buildings
items.note: The Golden Palace is open 08:00–16:00. The gold architecture is striking and photogenic from every angle. Dress modestly and remove your shoes where indicated.

items.activity: A closing lunch — back into town for giant gourami at one more spot
items.note: If you want to take giant gourami home, there are shops in town selling sun-dried gourami and dried goods to carry back.

items.activity: Pack up and drive back to Bangkok
items.note: Leaving in the early afternoon gets you to Bangkok before dark, dodging the evening holiday traffic just right.

blocks.title: What to know before visiting Wat Tha Sung
blocks.html: The Glass Temple opens in sessions: morning 09:00–11:30 and afternoon 14:00–16:00, while the rest of the grounds are open 08:00–16:00. To catch the Glass Temple in time, plan to reach the temple before 11:00 and dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered.

blocks.text: Tweak the plan to your style

items.name: If you have less time
items.blurb: With only two days, cut the nature day and focus on the riverside town and Wat Tha Sung. You'll finish comfortably without rushing.

items.name: All-in on nature
items.blurb: If you want to fully explore the Ban Rai–Lan Sak side, add more nature spots and caves in the same zone. See the separate nature plan.

items.name: Temples and culture
items.blurb: If you want to focus on temples and old town, add the riverside Wat Ubosatharam and other in-town temples. See the temples-and-culture plan.

blocks.text: Getting there and where to stay

items: From Bangkok — Drive the Asia Highway (Route 32), about 3 hours. This is the best fit because the middle day requires driving out to Ban Rai–Lan Sak, which public transport barely reaches.
Public transport — There are vans and buses from Mo Chit to Uthai Thani, but once you're in town, getting to Hub Pa Tat, Wat Tham Khao Wong, and up Khao Sakae Krang is hard. Rent a car in town.
Fuel up and prep — The nature day runs through the mountains with gas stations far apart. Fill the tank before you go and pack drinking water and snacks in the car.

Where to stay — Choose a hotel or floating house on the Sakae Krang in town and stay both nights in a row. You can walk to the morning market and Trok Rong Ya. See the curated picks on the hotel roundup page.

faq.q: What can you see in Uthai Thani in 3 days and 2 nights?
faq.a: It splits neatly into three parts. Day one is the Sakae Krang riverside town, walking Trok Rong Ya and heading up Khao Sakae Krang for sunset. Day two is the nature run, walking through the cave at Hub Pa Tat in Lan Sak and seeing Wat Tham Khao Wong in Ban Rai. Day three is the riverside morning market, then Wat Tha Sung before heading home. You get the town, nature, temples, and food.

faq.q: Where is Hub Pa Tat, what are the hours, and how much is entry?
faq.a: Hub Pa Tat is in Thung Na Ngam subdistrict, Lan Sak district, about 28 km from Uthai Thani town. It's open daily 08:00–16:30. Entry for Thai adults is 20 THB and children 10 THB. You walk through a limestone cave into a prehistoric forest valley thick with fan palms. Go mid-morning when the light pours into the valley.

faq.q: What are the hours for Wat Tham Khao Wong in Ban Rai?
faq.a: Wat Tham Khao Wong in Ban Rai district is open Monday–Friday 07:00–17:00 and Saturday–Sunday 07:00–18:00. The highlight is the multi-story Thai-style teakwood hall set in a limestone valley. You can walk up to the cave above, about 400 meters. Dress modestly and remove your shoes where indicated.

faq.q: Do you need your own car for the Uthai Thani nature route?
faq.a: The nature day does require your own car or a rental, because Hub Pa Tat is in Lan Sak and Wat Tham Khao Wong is in Ban Rai, both far from town and hard to reach by public transport. Fill the tank before you set off, since gas stations in the mountain zone are far apart.

faq.q: Where should you stay for a 3-day, 2-night Uthai Thani trip?
faq.a: Stay in town by the Sakae Krang River for both nights. You can walk to the morning market and Trok Rong Ya, and on the nature day you simply drive out and come back to the same bed without moving your bags. See the riverside stay options on the Uthai Thani hotel roundup page.
